summary: Uneven GPU balance causing intermittent p99 spikes and stream drops in dedicated pool
description: Issue summary: Beginning 2026-03-10 ~10:20 PDT BrightWrite observed repeated p95/p99 latency spikes (tokens/sec drop) and streaming connection resets for requests served from their dedicated GPU reservation. Impact: degraded customer real-time features, multiple 504/stream disconnects, and increased token costs due to replays. Timeline: 10:20-13:05 intermittent spikes with peak around 11:12. Environment: Dedicated GPU pool (reservation id: res-9c7), prod us-west, node type p4d-style. Observed behavior: sudden increase in per-request tail latency when certain long-sequence jobs enter the pool. While aggregate GPU utilization reported by cluster dashboards looked balanced, NVML sampling shows per-GPU compute / memory utilization was highly imbalanced (several GPUs at >92% while others idle), coincident with elevated context-switch rates and CUDA memory thrashing. Autoscaler did not provision new nodes quickly enough because it uses average queue length; queue skew meant some GPUs had long queues while overall queue was below scale threshold.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a dedicated reservation with mixed long-sequence (>=4096 tokens) and short-sequence requests from multiple tenants
2) Send a synthetic burst from tenant A with 12 concurrent long-sequence streaming requests while tenant B concurrently sends many short requests
3) Observe per-GPU queue lengths in /metrics/gpu_queue_length and tail latency in /metrics/latency_p99
4) Note streaming disconnects in application logs when individual GPU queue length > 50 for sustained 30s
logs: 2026-03-10T11:12:08Z [proxy] ERROR stream disconnect client_id=brightwrite-889 code=GRPC-504 description=upstream-write-failed
dmesg snippet: kernel: nvidia_uvm: process 8901 blocked on GPU memory mapping (OOM avoidance)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: noisy neighbor from long-sequence jobs causing localized GPU saturation and head-of-line blocking for short requests.
Correlated Datadog traces show that long-seq spans occupy same GPU IDs across multiple allocations — indicates affinity/scheduler packing behavior rather than random distribution.
Scheduler logs show affinity hinting code paths were exercised during a recent runtime rollout (PR 2491) — potential regression in packer that attempts to reduce cross-GPU migration.
Autoscaler tuning uses average queue length; in skewed distributions this under-reacts to hotspots. Observed scale decisions ignored max_queue_len spike.
No evidence of hardware failure; NVML reports healthy temperatures and no ECC errors. Pattern reproduced reliably with synthetic workload described above.
mitigation: Applied customer-side short-term workaround: set per-tenant max_concurrent_streams=6 to reduce long-seq concurrency (applied 2026-03-10T12:05).
Operator action: temporarily increased autoscaler sensitivity by lowering scale threshold to 15 and adding consideration for max_queue_len (applied 2026-03-10T12:20).
Isolated BrightWrite onto a different slice within their reservation to avoid co-hosting with other noisy long-sequence tenants (done 2026-03-10T12:45).
Rolled back a non-critical packer flag introduced in runtime PR 2491 to restore previous round-robin distribution while a fix is prepared (rolled back 2026-03-10T12:55).
resolution: Partial resolution implemented: per-tenant concurrency cap and autoscaler threshold change removed immediate tail spikes. Isolation of BrightWrite reduced impact to near-zero for the remainder of the day. Root cause tracked to two contributing factors: (1) a scheduler affinity regression in the runtime packer that favored co-locating long-seq jobs to reduce migrations, and (2) an autoscaler policy that relied on average queue length and ignored max_queue_len outliers. A code PR to make the packer respect a 'spread_long_sequences' flag and to add max_queue_len as a signal for scale-up was opened (PR 2518).
follow_up_actions: ENG-1: Merge fix PR for packer to avoid deterministic long-seq co-location and add test harness for mixed workloads (linked PR 2518).
OPS-1: Update autoscaler to consider max_queue_len and p99 latency signal for scale decisions (backlog ticket INT-4412).
DOC-1: Add runbook for dedicated-pool noisy-tenant incidents with steps for isolation and temp concurrency caps (confluence page updated).
CS-1: Schedule proactive outreach to BrightWrite to review workload shaping best practices and offer dedicated pinning options for extreme long-seq workloads.
